newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt up, focus on Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt up, focus on Ecuador.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mostly higher in late trade Monday as widespread talk of a $300 million five-year Eurobond for Ecuador pushed its Brady prices sharply higher, market sources said.
"The market is very strong. Talk of a Eurobond for Ecuador is pretty good news," said one emerging market trader at a major U.S. investment bank.

At 1645 EST/2145 GMT, Ecuadorean par bonds ECPARS=RR were one percentage point higher at 47-1/2 bid and its PDI bonds ECPDI=RR were 1-3/8 firmer at 60-5/8. The country's discount bonds ECDISC=RR were 1-1/8 stronger at 69-1/8.
Sources said market talk on the Ecuadorean Eurobond is between 350 to 390 basis points.
Chase Securities, which is said by market sources to be underwriting the issue, was not immediately available for comment.
Another factor that pushed Ecuador's debt higher was the release of the country's preliminary economic plan, which was reported in the local press on Sunday, another source said.

"I think the overall reception was quite positive on the Bradys," the source said. "Going though it, it seems fairly solid. Everything is as expected with regard to structural reforms and fiscal discipline."
Elsewhere, market sources said news out of Bulgaria was extremely positive and had added to the positive tone in the price of the country's debt.
Bulgaria's Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said the government and the central bank both agreed to the terms of the currency board plan proposed by the International Monetary Fund.
Under the currency board system, the exchange rate is pegged at a fixed level against a hard currency and money in circulation has to correspond to the official hard currency reserves at that rate.
Bulgaria's FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were 1-3/4 higher at 36-3/8 bid and the country's IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 1-5/8 better at 48-5/8 bid.
In the broader market, traders said prices were higher with U.S. Treasuries but activity was on the thin side.
"There has been some clients buying Bulgaria, Ecuador and Argentina but the rest of the countries are pretty quiet," said a trader.
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were 3/4 higher at 85-5/8 bid and Brazilian "C" bonds were 3/4 stronger at 72-1/2.
